candidate.blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance — infant safety and anticipatory guidance
candidate.blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — safe infant sleep
candidate.educational_objective: Teach evidence-based safe-sleep measures beyond supine positioning and a firm sleep surface.

options.A: Share an adult bed with the infant overnight for closer monitoring.
options.B: Place pillows and loose blankets in the sleep space to keep the infant warm.
options.C: Avoid smoke and nicotine exposure, prevent overheating, and offer a pacifier at naps and bedtime; if breastfeeding, wait until breastfeeding is established before introducing the pacifier.
options.D: Allow secondhand smoke exposure because it is not associated with SIDS risk.

candidate.rationale: Current CDC safe-sleep guidance explicitly supports the AAP 2022 recommendations: avoid smoke and nicotine exposure, avoid overheating, and offer a pacifier at naps and bedtime. For a breastfed infant, pacifier introduction should wait until breastfeeding is established. Adult bed-sharing and soft bedding are not recommended safe-sleep practices. C is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Avoid smoke/nicotine exposure and overheating; offer a pacifier at nap time and bedtime, delaying introduction until breastfeeding is established for breastfed infants; avoid bed-sharing and soft bedding.
candidate.source_document_title: Providing Care for Babies to Sleep Safely
candidate.source_locator: Creating a safe sleep area for babies; Additional recommendations to reduce the risk of SIDS
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), supporting American Academy of Pediatrics recommendations
candidate.stem: Which additional recommendation should the nurse include when teaching new parents how to reduce the risk of sleep-related infant death?
